Higashiyama-ku 63

Gion · Kiyomizu-dera · Sannenzaka · Kennin-ji · Yasaka · Tōfuku-ji

  1. Must see · Wagashi, Matcha & Sweets · Higashiyama-ku

    Kagizen Yoshifusa (鍵善良房)

    A Gion institution since the early 18th century; its tea room is the classic place for kuzukiri.

    264 Gionmachi Kitagawa, Higashiyama-ku, Kyoto

    Recommended by Time Out, Leaf Kyoto (京都リーフ), Lonely Planet, Inside Kyoto (Chris Rowthorn)

  2. Must see · Higashiyama-ku

    Kōdai-ji

    Founded 1606 by Nene in memory of Toyotomi Hideyoshi; a tsukiyama pond garden of man-made hills, pine and maple. Its sub-temple Entoku-in adds two more Zen gardens.

    Shimogawara-chō, Higashiyama-ku, Kyoto, Japan

    Recommended by Japan-guide, Wikipedia, Kyoto City Tourism

  3. Must see · Higashiyama-ku

    Kiyomizu-dera

    Eastern Kyoto's hillside temple, famous for the wooden terrace with a view over the city; part of the UNESCO 'Historic Monuments of Ancient Kyoto'.

    Look for 06:00–18:00 (to 18:30 Jul–Aug); 500 yen

    Kiyomizu, Higashiyama-ku, Kyoto, Japan

    Recommended by Japan-guide, Kyoto City Tourism

  4. Must see · Higashiyama-ku

    Higashiyama District (Sannenzaka & Ninenzaka)

    One of Kyoto's best-preserved historic districts — narrow lanes, wooden buildings and merchant shops on the 20–30 minute walk from Kiyomizu-dera to Yasaka Shrine.

    Higashiyama-ku, Kyoto, Japan

    Recommended by Japan-guide, Kyoto City Tourism

  5. Must see · Higashiyama-ku

    Yasaka Shrine (Yasaka-jinja)

    Gion's great shrine, home of the Gion Matsuri every July for over a thousand years; busiest at cherry-blossom time beside Maruyama Park.

    Gionmachi, Higashiyama-ku, Kyoto, Japan

    Recommended by Japan-guide, Kyoto City Tourism

  6. Must see · Higashiyama-ku

    Gion & Hanamikoji

    Kyoto's most famous geisha district, between Yasaka Shrine and the Kamo River — ochaya teahouses where geiko and maiko entertain.

    Gion, Higashiyama-ku, Kyoto, Japan

    Recommended by Japan-guide, Kyoto City Tourism

  7. Must see · Higashiyama-ku

    Chion-in

    Head temple of the Jōdo (Pure Land) sect; its Sanmon, 24 m tall and 50 m wide, is the largest wooden temple gate in Japan (early 1600s).

    Higashiyama-ku, Kyoto, Japan

    Recommended by Japan-guide, Kyoto City Tourism

  8. Must see · Higashiyama-ku

    Kennin-ji

    Founded 1202 — the oldest Zen temple in Kyoto, ranked third of the city's five great Zen temples, just south of Gion.

    Komatsu-chō (south of Gion), Higashiyama-ku, Kyoto, Japan

    Recommended by Japan-guide, Kyoto City Tourism

  9. Must see · Higashiyama-ku

    Tōfuku-ji

    One of the Kyoto Gozan (five great Zen temples), founded in the 13th century; its Tsūten-kyō bridge over a maple valley is one of Kyoto's most famous autumn-leaf views.

    15-778 Honmachi, Higashiyama-ku, Kyoto, Japan

    Recommended by Japan-guide, Ana Japan Travel Planner

  10. Must see · Higashiyama-ku

    Sanjūsangen-dō

    The 120-metre hall of 1266 (National Treasure) housing 1,001 standing Thousand-armed Kannon statues, flanked by Fūjin and Raijin.

    Higashiyama-ku, Kyoto, Japan

    Recommended by Wikipedia, Jta

  11. Must see · Soba & Udon · Higashiyama-ku

    Sōhonke Nishin Soba Matsuba

    Founded in 1861 as a theatre teahouse; in 1882 the second-generation owner invented nishin soba and moved beside the Minami-za kabuki theatre — the dish has been a Kyoto speciality ever since.

    Beside Minami-za, Shijō-dōri, Higashiyama-ku, Kyoto, Japan

    Recommended by Kyoto City Tourism, Japanese Wikipedia (ja.wikipedia.org)

  12. Must see · Wagashi, Matcha & Sweets · Higashiyama-ku

    Gion Tokuya (ぎおん徳屋)

    Gion's warabi-mochi specialist — the melt-in-the-mouth real-bracken version, with a queue to match.

    Gion, Higashiyama-ku, Kyoto

    Recommended by Time Out, Leaf Kyoto (京都リーフ)

  13. Must see · Sushi & Kaisen-don · Higashiyama-ku

    Gion Izuju (祇園 いづ重)

    A Kyō-zushi shop opposite Yasaka Shrine, founded in the late Meiji era by a former craftsman of Izuu who was given leave to open his own shop. Its saba-zushi uses true mackerel from the Sea of Japan.

    Gion, Higashiyama-ku, Kyoto (opposite Yasaka Shrine)

    Recommended by Rurubu (JTB Publishing, rurubu.jp), Wa-raku / intojapanwaraku (Shogakukan)

  14. Must see · Soba & Udon · Higashiyama-ku

    Gion Yorozuya

    Michelin Bib Gourmand udon house that began delivering meals to Gion teahouses and playhouses; queues form before opening for the onion udon heaped with Kyoto's Kujō spring onion.

    555-1 Komatsu-chō, Higashiyama-ku, Kyoto, Japan

    Recommended by Michelin Bib

  15. Must see · International & Fusion · Higashiyama-ku

    LURRA°

    One MICHELIN Star — innovative hearth cooking off Sanjō near Shirakawa, Kyoto-farm vegetables at the centre.

    396 Sekisenincho, Higashiyama-ku, Kyoto, 605-0021, Japan

    Recommended by Michelin ★

    Higashiyama Tsukasa

    One MICHELIN Star — the deep-fried roe-ayu roll was a 2026 inspectors' favourite dish.

    2F, 127 Nishimachi, Higashiyama-ku, Kyoto, 605-0037, Japan

    Recommended by Michelin ★

    463-30 Shimokawaracho, Higashiyama-ku, Kyoto, 605-0825, Japan

    Recommended by Michelin ★

    One MICHELIN Star sushi counter produced by Gion Sasaki.

    Jean-Georges at The Shinmonzen

  21. Must see · Wagyu, Yakiniku & Sukiyaki · Higashiyama-ku

    Kodaiji Jugyuan

    Two MICHELIN Stars — in a century-old sukiya house near Kōdai-ji; the grilled wagyu is an inspectors' must-try.

    353 Masuyacho, Higashiyama-ku, Kyoto, 605-0826, Japan

    Recommended by Michelin ★

  22. Must see · Sushi & Kaisen-don · Higashiyama-ku

    Izuu

    Founded in 1781 when salted Wakasa mackerel made saba-zushi Kyoto's festival food; the eighth-generation chef still presses whole-mackerel sushi (Michelin Bib Gourmand).

    367 Kiyomoto-chō, Higashiyama-ku, Kyoto 605-0084, Japan

    Recommended by Michelin Bib

    566-27 Komatsu-chō, Higashiyama-ku, Kyoto 605-0811, Japan

    Recommended by Michelin ★

    Kikunoi Honten

    Three MICHELIN Stars (2026). Opened as a restaurant in 1912 and now run by the third-generation chef, it keeps Kyoto's culinary traditions while adding Western ingredients.

    459 Shimokawara-chō, Higashiyama-ku, Kyoto 605-0825, Japan

    Recommended by Michelin ★

    Two MICHELIN Stars Japanese (kaiseki) restaurant in Gion.

    Higashiyama Yoshihisa

    422 Myōhōin Maekawa-chō, Higashiyama-ku, Kyoto 605-0932, Japan

    Recommended by Michelin ★

  29. Must see · Sushi & Kaisen-don · Higashiyama-ku

    Kanesho

    Michelin Bib Gourmand eel house founded at the end of the Edo period as a river-fish wholesaler; the fourth-generation chef's kinshi-don, under thin-cut omelette ribbons, is renowned.

    155-2 Tokiwa-chō, Higashiyama-ku, Kyoto 605-0079, Japan

    Recommended by Michelin Bib

  30. Must see · Kaiseki, Kyō-ryōri & Ryōtei · Higashiyama-ku

    Recommended by Michelin ★

  31. Worth the detour · Higashiyama-ku

    Maruyama Park

    Public park next to Yasaka Shrine; in early April Kyoto's most popular (and most crowded) hanami spot under the weeping cherry.

    Higashiyama-ku, Kyoto, Japan

    Recommended by Japan-guide, Kyoto City Tourism

  32. Worth the detour · Higashiyama-ku

    Shōren-in

    Tendai monzeki temple whose head priests were traditionally imperial; houses the National Treasure painting of the Blue Cetaka (Ao Fudō) and a garden attributed to Sōami.

    Awataguchi, Higashiyama-ku, Kyoto, Japan

    Recommended by Japan-guide, Kyoto City Tourism

  33. Worth the detour · Higashiyama-ku

    Hōkan-ji (Yasaka Pagoda)

    The five-storey Yasaka Pagoda rising over the Higashiyama lanes on the walk up to Kiyomizu-dera.

    Yasaka, Higashiyama-ku, Kyoto, Japan

    Recommended by Kyoto City Tourism, Wikipedia

  34. Worth the detour · Higashiyama-ku

    Rokuharamitsu-ji

    Founded in 951 by the itinerant monk Kūya — the 17th temple of the Saigoku Kannon pilgrimage — in Rokuhara, the old Heike warrior quarter; its Kūya statue shows tiny Buddhas issuing from his mouth.

    2-81-1 Rokuhara-chō, Higashiyama-ku, Kyoto 605-0813, Japan

    Recommended by Wikipedia, Kyoto National Museum

  35. Worth the detour · Higashiyama-ku

    Kyoto National Museum

    One of Japan's four national museums, in the Higashiyama temple district opposite Sanjūsangen-dō; Kyoto's major collection of pre-modern Japanese and Asian art.

    Higashiyama-ku, Kyoto, Japan

    Recommended by Japan-guide, Kyoto Museums Council (kyoto-museums.jp)

  36. Worth the detour · Higashiyama-ku

    Chishaku-in

    Head temple of the Chisan school of Shingon Buddhism, opposite the Kyoto National Museum; known for its early-Edo pond garden and Momoyama-period Hasegawa school screen paintings that are National Treasures.

    Higashiyama-ku, Kyoto, Japan

    Recommended by Wikipedia, Kyoto City Tourism

  37. Worth the detour · Higashiyama-ku

    Sennyū-ji

    Imperial family temple ('Mitera') whose origin traces to the 820s–830s, with imperial mausolea in its wooded precinct below Tōfuku-ji; head of the Sennyū-ji branch of Shingon.

    Higashiyama-ku, Kyoto, Japan

    Recommended by Wikipedia, Kyoto City Tourism

  38. Worth the detour · Higashiyama-ku

    Yasui Konpira-gū

    Shrine for cutting bad ties and binding good ones: crawl through the hole in the paper-covered 'enkiri-enmusubi' stone to make your wish.

    Higashiyama-ku, Kyoto, Japan

    Recommended by Kyoto City Tourism, Japanese Wikipedia (ja.wikipedia.org)

  39. Worth the detour · Higashiyama-ku

    Rokudō Chinnō-ji

    Temple at the old 'crossroads of the six realms' by the Toribeno burial ground; its well is said to be where the courtier Ono no Takamura descended nightly to the underworld.

    Higashiyama-ku, Kyoto, Japan

    Recommended by Kyoto City Tourism, Japanese Wikipedia (ja.wikipedia.org)

  40. Worth the detour · Higashiyama-ku

    Entoku-in

    Kōdai-ji sub-temple built after 1605 by Nene, Hideyoshi's widow, where she spent her last years — two rock gardens and painted screens.

    Higashiyama-ku, Kyoto, Japan

    Recommended by Japan-guide, Japanese Wikipedia (ja.wikipedia.org)

  41. Worth the detour · Higashiyama-ku

    Toyokuni Shrine

    Shrine to Toyotomi Hideyoshi, prayed at for career success; its karamon gate with carved carp and cranes is a National Treasure. Next to Hōkō-ji's great bell.

    Higashiyama-ku, Kyoto, Japan

    Recommended by Kyoto City Tourism, Japanese Wikipedia (ja.wikipedia.org)

  42. Worth the detour · Izakaya, Yakitori & Yokochō · Higashiyama-ku

    Gyoza Hohei (ぎょうざ 歩兵)

    Gion's beloved gyoza counter (a past Bib Gourmand, 2017 on) — Kyoto's answer to the after-hours dumpling.

    Gion, Higashiyama-ku, Kyoto

    Recommended by Time Out, Inside Kyoto (Chris Rowthorn)

  43. Worth the detour · Wagashi, Matcha & Sweets · Higashiyama-ku

    Bunnosuke Chaya Kyoto Honten (京甘味 文の助茶屋 京都本店)

    A sweet house founded in 1909; the classic warabi-mochi stop on the Kiyomizu approach.

    Near Sannenzaka / Yasaka, Higashiyama-ku, Kyoto

    Recommended by Kyoto City Tourism, Leaf Kyoto (京都リーフ)

  44. Worth the detour · Wagashi, Matcha & Sweets · Higashiyama-ku

    Kasagiya (かさぎ屋)

    The most atmospheric little tea house in Kyoto, beside the stone steps at the top of Ninenzaka.

    349 Masuya-chō, Kōdai-ji, Higashiyama-ku, Kyoto (top of Ninenzaka steps)

    Recommended by Inside Kyoto (Chris Rowthorn), Matcha — Japan Travel Guide

  45. Worth the detour · Soba & Udon · Higashiyama-ku

    Gion Okaru (祇園 おかる)

    A low-key Gion udon shop popular with geiko and maiko. It is known for its curry udon and stays open until 2–3 a.m., so it is a usual stop after a night out.

    Gion, Higashiyama-ku, Kyoto (short walk from Gion-Shijō Station)

    Recommended by Inside Kyoto (Chris Rowthorn), Leaf Kyoto (京都リーフ)

  46. Worth the detour · Wagashi, Matcha & Sweets · Higashiyama-ku

    Gion Komori (ぎをん小森)

    A sweets parlour in a former Gion teahouse on the Shirakawa canal. It makes its warabi-mochi by hand each morning and uses Tokachi Dainagon azuki and Yoshino kuzu.

    Shinbashi-dōri, Gion, Higashiyama-ku, Kyoto (beside the Shirakawa canal)

    Recommended by Walkerplus (kadokawa), Leaf Kyoto (京都リーフ)

    Gojōzaka, Higashiyama-ku, Kyoto (on the Kiyomizu-dera approach)

    Recommended by Rurubu (JTB Publishing, rurubu.jp), Walkerplus (kadokawa)

  63. Deep cut · Higashiyama-ku

    Mimizuka

    The 'Ear Mound' — a sobering burial mound for the ears and noses taken as trophies from Korean and Chinese soldiers in Hideyoshi's 1590s invasions of Korea; a national Historic Site.

    533-1 Chaya-chō, Higashiyama-ku, Kyoto, Japan

Sakyō-ku 50

Ginkaku-ji · Philosopher's Path · Nanzen-ji · Okazaki · Demachiyanagi · Shimogamo

  1. Must see · Sakyō-ku

    Philosopher's Path

    Two-kilometre canal-side stone path from Ginkaku-ji to the Nanzen-ji neighbourhood, named for philosopher Nishida Kitarō's daily meditative walk; lined with cherry trees.

    Sakyō-ku, Kyoto, Japan

    Recommended by Japan-guide, Kyoto City Tourism, Wikipedia

  2. Must see · Sakyō-ku

    Eikan-dō (Zenrin-ji)

    Jōdo temple north of Nanzen-ji, among Kyoto's most famous autumn-colour spots with evening illuminations in November; known for its 'looking-back' Amida statue.

    Sakyō-ku, Kyoto, Japan

    Recommended by Japan-guide, Kyoto City Tourism, Wikipedia

  3. Must see · Sakyō-ku

    Heian Jingū

    Shrine built in 1895 for the 1,100th anniversary of the capital, its giant vermilion torii towering over Okazaki; the stroll garden behind is one of Kyoto's best for weeping cherry trees.

    Sakyō-ku, Kyoto, Japan

    Recommended by Japan-guide, Kyoto City Tourism, Wikipedia

  4. Must see · Tofu, Shōjin & Vegetarian · Sakyō-ku

    Nanzenji Junsei (南禅寺 順正)

    The classic Nanzen-ji yudofu house, set in an Edo-period medical-school building and garden by the temple gate.

    In front of Nanzen-ji's Sanmon gate, Sakyō-ku, Kyoto

    Recommended by Leaf Kyoto (京都リーフ), Kyoto City Tourism, Inside Kyoto (Chris Rowthorn)

  5. Must see · Tofu, Shōjin & Vegetarian · Sakyō-ku

    Okutan Nanzen-ji (奥丹 南禅寺)

    Has served Zen-temple tofu for centuries in a garden just outside Nanzen-ji — the most atmospheric yudofu in town.

    Beside Nanzen-ji, Sakyō-ku, Kyoto (garden of Chōshō-in)

    Recommended by Lonely Planet, Inside Kyoto (Chris Rowthorn), Kyoto City Tourism

  6. Must see · Sakyō-ku

    Nanzen-ji

    Head temple of the Nanzen-ji school of Rinzai Zen at the foot of the Higashiyama hills — the massive Sanmon gate, Hōjō rock garden and the brick Meiji-era Lake Biwa Canal aqueduct running through the grounds.

    Sakyō-ku, Kyoto, Japan

    Recommended by Japan-guide, Wikipedia

  7. Must see · Sakyō-ku

    Shimogamo Shrine (Kamo-mioya Jinja)

    Ancient shrine at the meeting of the Kamo and Takano rivers, reached through the Tadasu-no-Mori primeval forest; UNESCO-listed component 688-002.

    Sakyō-ku, Kyoto, Japan

    Recommended by UNESCO, Wikipedia

  8. Must see · Sakyō-ku

    Ginkaku-ji (Jishō-ji)

    The Silver Pavilion, Ashikaga Yoshimasa's retirement villa turned Zen temple, with its raked-sand garden and moss paths at the head of the Philosopher's Path; UNESCO 688-014.

    Sakyō-ku, Kyoto, Japan

    Recommended by UNESCO, Wikipedia

  9. Must see · Ramen & Tsukemen · Sakyō-ku

    Chūka Soba Takayasu (中華そば 高安)

    The originator of the cloudy, creamy-but-not-greasy broth that defines the Ichijōji ramen battleground; soup simmered 22+ hours.

    Ichijōji, Sakyō-ku, Kyoto (Ichijōji ramen street)

    Recommended by Leaf Kyoto (京都リーフ), Savor Japan

  10. Must see · Soba & Udon · Sakyō-ku

    Omen Ginkakuji Honten (名代おめん 銀閣寺本店)

    Since 1967 the Philosopher's-Path udon stop: thick noodles dipped in hot broth with a tray of condiments.

    Below Ginkaku-ji (3 min from Ginkakuji-mae bus stop), Sakyō-ku, Kyoto

    Recommended by Inside Kyoto (Chris Rowthorn), Leaf Kyoto (京都リーフ)

  11. Must see · Ramen & Tsukemen · Sakyō-ku

    Menya Gokkei (麺屋 極鶏), Ichijōji

    The most famous queue on Ichijōji ramen street: a chicken broth so thick it coats the spoon.

    Ichijōji ramen street, Sakyō-ku, Kyoto

    Recommended by Matcha — Japan Travel Guide, Leaf Kyoto (京都リーフ)

  12. Must see · Wagashi, Matcha & Sweets · Sakyō-ku

    Kamo Mitarashi Chaya (加茂みたらし茶屋), Shimogamo

    A teahouse founded in 1922 outside Shimogamo Shrine, widely called the birthplace of mitarashi dango. The dumplings imitate the bubbles rising in the shrine's Mitarashi pond, and the shop is said to have created the sweet-soy glaze.

    Shimogamo, Sakyō-ku, Kyoto (by the gate of Shimogamo Shrine)

    Recommended by Wa-raku / intojapanwaraku (Shogakukan), co-trip (Shobunsha)

  13. Must see · Ramen & Tsukemen · Sakyō-ku

    Ramen Touhichi

    Michelin Bib Gourmand ramen shop in Ichijōji; the signature soy-sauce ramen uses a dashi of locally raised free-range chicken and water only, finished with a raw soy-sauce kaeshi.

    8-6 Yamabana Itchoda-chō, Sakyō-ku, Kyoto 606-8007, Japan

    Recommended by Michelin Bib

  14. Must see · Soba & Udon · Sakyō-ku

    Kyoudon Kisoba Okakita

    Michelin Bib Gourmand udon-and-soba house on the Heian Jingū approach in Okazaki, serving soft Kyoto-style udon in light dashi.

    34 Okazaki Minamigosho-chō, Sakyō-ku, Kyoto 606-8334, Japan

    Recommended by Michelin Bib

  15. Must see · Kaiseki, Kyō-ryōri & Ryōtei · Sakyō-ku

    Hyotei

    Three MICHELIN Stars (2026) — a veteran ryōtei by Nanzen-ji whose rooms breathe wabi-sabi restraint.

    35 Nanzenji Kusagawa-chō, Sakyō-ku, Kyoto 606-8437, Japan

    Recommended by Michelin ★

  16. Must see · Kaiseki, Kyō-ryōri & Ryōtei · Sakyō-ku

    Kyokaiseki Kichisen

    Two MICHELIN Stars kyō-kaiseki house in Shimogamo.

    5 Shimogamo Morimoto-chō, Sakyō-ku, Kyoto 606-0805, Japan

    Recommended by Michelin ★

  17. Worth the detour · Sakyō-ku

    Murin-an

    Statesman Yamagata Aritomo's 1894 villa with a lawn-and-stream garden by Ogawa Jihei borrowing the Higashiyama hills; a nationally designated Place of Scenic Beauty.

    Sakyō-ku, Kyoto, Japan

    Recommended by Agency For Cultural Affairs, Kyoto City Tourism, Wikipedia

  18. Worth the detour · Sakyō-ku

    Enkō-ji (圓光寺)

    Zen temple founded by Tokugawa Ieyasu in 1600: the Honryū-tei dry 'Dragon Garden', a pond stroll garden, a small bamboo grove and a hilltop view.

    13 Ichijōji Kotani-chō, Sakyō-ku, Kyoto

    Recommended by Lonely Planet, Inside Kyoto (Chris Rowthorn), Japanese Wikipedia (ja.wikipedia.org)

  19. Worth the detour · Sakyō-ku

    Yoshida Shrine (吉田神社)

    The largest shrine on Yoshida-yama above Kyoto University, famous for its Setsubun fire festival.

    30 Yoshida Kaguraoka-chō, Sakyō-ku, Kyoto

    Recommended by Lonely Planet, Kyoto City Tourism, Japanese Wikipedia (ja.wikipedia.org)

  20. Worth the detour · Sakyō-ku

    Konkai Kōmyō-ji / Kurodani (金戒光明寺)

    A large Jōdo temple on Yoshida-yama hill near the Philosopher's Path, loved by locals for strolls and rarely busy with tourists; its huge San-mon gate is a frequent film location.

    Kurodani-chō, Sakyō-ku, Kyoto

    Recommended by Japanese Wikipedia (ja.wikipedia.org), Inside Kyoto (Chris Rowthorn), Lonely Planet

  21. Worth the detour · Sakyō-ku

    Keibunsha Ichijōji (恵文社一乗寺店)

    An independent bookshop opened in 1975 and regarded as the forerunner of Kyoto's independent bookstores, with curated books, a gallery and lifestyle goods.

    Ichijōji, Sakyō-ku, Kyoto

    Recommended by Japanese Wikipedia (ja.wikipedia.org), Kyoto City Tourism, Rurubu (JTB Publishing, rurubu.jp)

  22. Worth the detour · Kissaten & Coffee · Sakyō-ku

    Blue Bottle Coffee Kyoto Cafe, Nanzen-ji

    Blue Bottle's first Kansai café, opened in 2018 in a renovated machiya more than 100 years old near Nanzen-ji. Its reservation-only floor is the only one in Japan.

    64 Nanzenji Kusakawa-chō, Sakyō-ku, Kyoto

    Recommended by Leaf Kyoto (京都リーフ), Rurubu (JTB Publishing, rurubu.jp), Kyoto Shimbun

  23. Worth the detour · Sakyō-ku

    Hōnen-in

    Quiet temple just off the Philosopher's Path with a moss-thatched gate and raked sand mounds — the most notable temple on the walk, especially in autumn.

    Sakyō-ku, Kyoto, Japan

    Recommended by Japan-guide, Wikipedia

  24. Worth the detour · Sakyō-ku

    Kyoto City KYOCERA Museum of Art

    Opened in 1933 as the Enthronement Memorial Museum — Japan's oldest public art museum still in its original building, renovated by Jun Aoki; Okazaki Park.

    Sakyō-ku, Kyoto, Japan

    Recommended by Kyoto City Tourism, Wikipedia

  25. Worth the detour · Sakyō-ku

    National Museum of Modern Art, Kyoto

    Fumihiko Maki-designed national museum facing the KYOCERA across the Heian Jingū approach, strong on Kyoto-school painting and modern ceramics (Kawai Kanjirō).

    Sakyō-ku, Kyoto, Japan

    Recommended by Kyoto City Tourism, Wikipedia

  26. Worth the detour · Sakyō-ku

    Konchi-in

    Nanzen-ji sub-temple whose crane-and-turtle garden by Kobori Enshū is a Special Place of Scenic Beauty.

    Sakyō-ku, Kyoto, Japan

    Recommended by Agency For Cultural Affairs, Wikipedia

  27. Worth the detour · Sakyō-ku

    Shugakuin Imperial Villa

    Retired Emperor Go-Mizunoo's 1655 hillside villa of three gardens stepped among rice terraces at the foot of Mount Hiei; free Imperial Household Agency tours by reservation; Special Place of Scenic Beauty.

    Sakyō-ku, Kyoto, Japan

    Recommended by Agency For Cultural Affairs, Wikipedia

  28. Worth the detour · Sakyō-ku

    Shisen-dō

    The 'Hall of Immortal Poets', a scholar-poet's 1641 mountain hermitage hung with portraits of 36 Chinese poets, looking onto a white-sand garden of clipped azaleas and maples.

    Sakyō-ku, Kyoto, Japan

    Recommended by Kyoto City Tourism, Wikipedia

  29. Worth the detour · Sakyō-ku

    Manshu-in

    Tendai monzeki temple near Shugakuin, 'almost a temple within a garden': a sea of raked white gravel with islands of trees, rock and moss.

    Sakyō-ku, Kyoto, Japan

    Recommended by Kyoto City Tourism, Wikipedia

  30. Worth the detour · Sakyō-ku

    Shinnyo-dō

    Tendai temple founded in 984 on the Yoshida hills, its pagoda and maples one of Kyoto's quieter famous autumn-leaf spots.

    Sakyō-ku, Kyoto, Japan

    Recommended by Kyoto City Tourism, Wikipedia

  31. Worth the detour · Sakyō-ku

    Kyoto Botanical Gardens

    Large public botanical garden in Kitayama by the Kamo River, with a big conservatory and seasonal flower collections.

    Sakyō-ku, Kyoto, Japan

    Recommended by Kyoto City Tourism, Wikipedia

  32. Worth the detour · Sakyō-ku

    Keage Incline

    Disused inclined railway of the Meiji-era Lake Biwa Canal that hauled boats until the 1950s; the tracks are now a walk under about a hundred cherry trees.

    Sakyō-ku, Kyoto, Japan

    Recommended by Japan-guide, Wikipedia

  33. Worth the detour · Sakyō-ku

    Hakusasonsō Hashimoto Kansetsu Garden & Museum (白沙村荘)

    Former home and studio of Taishō–Shōwa painter Hashimoto Kansetsu: a pond-stroll garden framed by Mt Daimonji, a National Place of Scenic Beauty, with a museum of his work and collection.

    Jōdo-ji, Sakyō-ku, Kyoto

    Recommended by Japanese Wikipedia (ja.wikipedia.org), Kyoto City Tourism

  34. Worth the detour · Ramen & Tsukemen · Sakyō-ku

    Tenkaippin Sōhonten (天下一品 総本店)

    The original shop of the nationwide kotteri chain, often credited with starting Ichijōji's ramen boom. Fans hold that the broth is still best here.

    Sakyō-ku, Kyoto (Ichijōji ramen district; ~15 min walk from Ichijōji Station)

    Recommended by byFood (byfood.com), Good Luck Trip (gltjp.com)

  35. Worth the detour · Ramen & Tsukemen · Sakyō-ku

    Tentenyū (天天有), Ichijōji

    One of the oldest shops on the Ichijōji ramen strip, open since 1971 and late into the night. It is known for its slow-simmered chicken broth.

    49 Ichijōji Nishisuginomiya-chō, Sakyō-ku, Kyoto (5 min walk from Ichijōji Station)

    Recommended by Mapple (Shobunsha), byFood (byfood.com)

  36. Worth the detour · International & Fusion · Sakyō-ku

    Pizzeria da Ciro

    Bib Gourmand pizzeria near Ginkaku-ji — the chef imported an Italian oven-builder for his oven.

    75 Jodoji Nishidacho, Sakyo-ku, Kyoto, 606-8417, Japan

    Recommended by Michelin Bib

  37. Worth the detour · Sushi & Kaisen-don · Sakyō-ku

    Shimogamo Ichima

    MICHELIN-listed Shimogamo sushi house keeping the bite-size temari-zushi tradition alive.

    93-1 Shimogamo Nishihangicho, Sakyo-ku, Kyoto, 606-0827, Japan

    Recommended by Michelin

  38. Worth the detour · Soba & Udon · Sakyō-ku

    Juu-go

    Michelin Bib Gourmand soba restaurant in the Jōdo-ji quarter near Ginkaku-ji.

    71-6 Jōdoji Kamiminamida-chō, Sakyō-ku, Kyoto 606-8405, Japan

    Recommended by Michelin Bib

  39. Worth the detour · International & Fusion · Sakyō-ku

    Kyo Seika

    One MICHELIN Star Chinese restaurant in Okazaki cooking with a seasonal Kyoto aesthetic.

    2F, 36-3 Okazaki Enshōji-chō, Sakyō-ku, Kyoto 606-8344, Japan

    Recommended by Michelin ★

  40. Worth the detour · Kaiseki, Kyō-ryōri & Ryōtei · Sakyō-ku

    Higashiyama Ogata

    One MICHELIN Star offshoot of Ogata where its apprentices cook — known for hot-pots and dishes grilled over a shichirin brazier.

    91-5 Okazaki Enshōji-chō, Sakyō-ku, Kyoto 606-8344, Japan

    Recommended by Michelin ★

  41. Deep cut · Sakyō-ku

    Takaragaike Park (宝が池公園)

    Edo-period agricultural reservoir turned popular park with a lakeside running loop and the Kodomo no Rakuen children's play area.

    Kamitakano, Sakyō-ku, Kyoto

    Recommended by Japanese Wikipedia (ja.wikipedia.org), Matcha — Japan Travel Guide, Kyoto City Tourism

  42. Deep cut · Sakyō-ku

    Sekizan Zen-in (赤山禅院)

    Tendai temple at the western foot of Mt Hiei, founded in 864 by Ennin's disciple An'e and rebuilt in 884, enshrining the deity Sekizan Myōjin.

    Shūgakuin, Sakyō-ku, Kyoto

    Recommended by Japanese Wikipedia (ja.wikipedia.org), Wikipedia

  43. Deep cut · Sakyō-ku

    Hosomi Museum (細見美術館)

    Private art museum of the industrialist Hosomi family's collection spanning Shintō and Buddhist art, tea-ceremony objects and Edo-period painting.

    Okazaki, Sakyō-ku, Kyoto

    Recommended by Japanese Wikipedia (ja.wikipedia.org), Matcha — Japan Travel Guide

  44. Deep cut · Sakyō-ku

    Konpuku-ji (金福寺)

    Small Rinzai temple founded 864; Matsuo Bashō stayed in a thatched hut in its garden, later named Bashō-an.

    Ichijōji, Sakyō-ku, Kyoto

    Recommended by Japanese Wikipedia (ja.wikipedia.org), Wikipedia

  45. Deep cut · Sakyō-ku

    Ōtoyo Shrine (大豊神社)

    Small shrine just off the Philosopher's Path whose sub-shrine to Ōkuninushi is guarded by komainu mice instead of dogs or foxes.

    Shishigatani, Sakyō-ku, Kyoto

    Recommended by Japanese Wikipedia (ja.wikipedia.org), Inside Kyoto (Chris Rowthorn)

  46. Deep cut · Sakyō-ku

    Anraku-ji (安楽寺)

    Tiny temple off the Philosopher's Path, open to the public only on limited days — worth it if you are in town when it opens.

    Shishigatani, Sakyō-ku, Kyoto

    Recommended by Japanese Wikipedia (ja.wikipedia.org), Inside Kyoto (Chris Rowthorn)

  47. Deep cut · Sakyō-ku

    Kyoto City Zoo (京都市動物園)

    Opened 1903 as Japan's second zoo, in Okazaki a short walk from Heian Jingū and Nanzen-ji.

    Okazaki, Sakyō-ku, Kyoto

    Recommended by Japanese Wikipedia (ja.wikipedia.org), Kyoto City Tourism

  48. Deep cut · Sakyō-ku

    Nomura Art Museum (野村美術館)

    Museum of scrolls, paintings, tea-ceremony implements and ceramics bequeathed by the business magnate Nomura.

    Nanzen-ji area, Sakyō-ku, Kyoto

    Recommended by Japanese Wikipedia (ja.wikipedia.org), Lonely Planet

  49. Deep cut · Sakyō-ku

    Kyoto University Museum (京都大学総合博物館)

    Kyoto University's museum on the Yoshida campus, listed by the city's school-trip guide among its university museums.

    Yoshida-honmachi, Sakyō-ku, Kyoto

    Recommended by Japanese Wikipedia (ja.wikipedia.org), Kyoto City Tourism

  50. Deep cut · International & Fusion · Sakyō-ku

    Bistro Cerisier

    Michelin Bib Gourmand French regional bistro in Tanaka — fish soup, goat's-cheese salad, sautéed frog.

    1-3 Tanaka Shimoyanagi-chō, Sakyō-ku, Kyoto 606-8204, Japan

    Recommended by Michelin Bib

Central 82

Nakagyō & Shimogyō (Nishiki · Pontochō · Kawaramachi · Karasuma · Nijō Castle · Kyoto Station

  1. Must see · Central

    Nishiki Market

    'Kyoto's Kitchen' — a narrow five-block covered street of more than a hundred food shops (the first opened around 1310): pickles, fresh yuba, dashi-maki tamago, seasonal Kyoto produce and knives.

    Nakagyō-ku, Kyoto, Japan

    Recommended by Japan-guide, Kyoto City Tourism, Wikipedia

  2. Must see · Central

    Pontochō

    Lantern-lit lane of teahouses and restaurants squeezed between the Kamo River and Kiyamachi — one of Kyoto's five geisha districts, with summer kawayuka dining platforms over the river.

    Nakagyō-ku, Kyoto, Japan

    Recommended by Japan-guide, Kyoto City Tourism, Wikipedia

  3. Must see · Central

    Higashi Hongan-ji

    Head temple of the Ōtani branch of Jōdo Shinshū near Kyoto Station; its Goeidō founder's hall is Kyoto's largest wooden structure. Free to enter.

    Shimogyō-ku, Kyoto, Japan

    Recommended by Japan-guide, Kyoto City Tourism, Wikipedia

  4. Must see · Central

    Kyoto Railway Museum

    JR West's museum (2016) by Umekōji Park with more than 50 retired trains, from steam locomotives in a working roundhouse to shinkansen; closed Wednesdays.

    Shimogyō-ku, Kyoto, Japan

    Recommended by Japan-guide, Kyoto City Tourism, Wikipedia

  5. Must see · Central

    Kyoto International Manga Museum

    Japan's first manga museum, in a 1929 elementary-school building by Karasuma-Oike Station, with some 300,000 items and walls of manga you can pull down and read.

    Nakagyō-ku, Kyoto, Japan

    Recommended by Japan-guide, Kyoto City Tourism, Wikipedia

  6. Must see · Wagashi, Matcha & Sweets · Central

    Imanishiken (今西軒), Gojō

    An ohagi shop founded in 1897 using Tokachi azuki and Shiga mochi rice, which often sells out within an hour of opening.

    Near Gojō Station, Shimogyō-ku, Kyoto

    Recommended by Leaf Kyoto (京都リーフ), Rurubu (JTB Publishing, rurubu.jp), Mapple (Shobunsha)

  7. Must see · Central

    Nishi Hongan-ji

    Head temple of the Jōdo Shinshū Hongwanji-ha, a short walk from Kyoto Station, with vast Founder's and Amida halls and Momoyama-era gates; UNESCO 688-016.

    Shimogyō-ku, Kyoto, Japan

    Recommended by UNESCO, Wikipedia

  8. Must see · Central

    Nijō Castle

    The Tokugawa shoguns' Kyoto residence (1603), whose Ninomaru Palace 'nightingale floors' chirp underfoot; UNESCO 688-017.

    Nakagyō-ku, Kyoto, Japan

    Recommended by UNESCO, Wikipedia

  9. Must see · Ramen & Tsukemen · Central

    Honke Daiichi-Asahi Takabashi

    The Takabashi ramen institution founded in 1947, five minutes' walk from Kyoto Station — the benchmark for Kyoto's soy-pork-bone style.

    845 Higashishiokōji Mukaihata-chō, Shimogyō-ku, Kyoto 600-8216, Japan

    Recommended by Leaf Kyoto (京都リーフ), Culture Trip

  10. Must see · Kissaten & Coffee · Central

    Inoda Coffee Honten

    Kyoto's classic kissaten, in business since 1940; the retro main shop serves a 'Kyoto breakfast' available only at the flagship.

    140 Dōyū-chō, Sakaimachi-dōri Sanjō-sagaru, Nakagyō-ku, Kyoto 604-8118, Japan

    Recommended by Kyoto City Tourism, Japanese Wikipedia (ja.wikipedia.org)

  11. Must see · Soba & Udon · Central

    Honke Owariya

    Founded in 1465 and billed as Japan's oldest soba restaurant; stock made with Kyoto well water and freshly boiled buckwheat noodles.

    Nakagyō-ku, Kyoto, Japan

    Recommended by Kyoto City Tourism, Time Out

  12. Must see · Kissaten & Coffee · Central

    François Kissashitsu (フランソア喫茶室)

    Kyoto's iconic 1934 meikyoku-kissa; in 2003 the first café in Japan registered as a national Tangible Cultural Property.

    Nishikiyamachi-dōri by the Takase-gawa, Shimogyō-ku, Kyoto (1 min from Kyoto-Kawaramachi Stn)

    Recommended by Kyoto City Tourism, Leaf Kyoto (京都リーフ)

  13. Must see · Kissaten & Coffee · Central

    Rokuyōsha (六曜社珈琲店)

    Family-run since 1950 at Sanjō-Kawaramachi — two floors, two coffees; a cornerstone of Kyoto's kissaten culture.

    Sanjō-Kawaramachi, Nakagyō-ku, Kyoto

    Recommended by Lonely Planet, Leaf Kyoto (京都リーフ)

  14. Must see · Ramen & Tsukemen · Central

    Menya Inoichi (麺屋 猪一)

    A 10-seat downtown counter whose 100% seafood broth is the anti-kotteri Kyoto bowl; Leaf KYOTO reports nine straight years of Michelin Bib Gourmand.

    Kawaramachi, Shimogyō-ku, Kyoto

    Recommended by Leaf Kyoto (京都リーフ), Inside Kyoto (Chris Rowthorn)

  15. Must see · Kaiseki, Kyō-ryōri & Ryōtei · Central

    Kikunoi Roan (菊乃井 露庵)

    Two MICHELIN Stars (2026): the Kikunoi house's counter restaurant — Inside Kyoto calls it the more affordable, less orthodox of the two.

    118 Saitō-chō, Shimogyō-ku, Kyoto 600-8012

    Recommended by Michelin ★, Inside Kyoto (Chris Rowthorn)

  16. Must see · Kissaten & Coffee · Central

    Smart Coffee (スマート珈琲店)

    Retro Teramachi-arcade kissaten serving since 1932 — the French toast has been on the menu for 50 years.

    537 Tenshōjimae-chō, Teramachi-dōri Sanjō-agaru, Nakagyō-ku, Kyoto

    Recommended by Inside Kyoto (Chris Rowthorn), Leaf Kyoto (京都リーフ)

  17. Must see · Kaiseki, Kyō-ryōri & Ryōtei · Central

    Muromachi Yui

    Two MICHELIN Stars (promoted 2026) — kyō-ryōri in the Muromachi quarter; the abalone appetiser is an inspectors' favourite.

    459 Kimbukicho, Nakagyo-ku, Kyoto, 604-0846, Japan

    Recommended by Michelin ★

  18. Must see · International & Fusion · Central

    Korean Restaurant Byeoleeya

    New One MICHELIN Star 2026 — Korean royal court cuisine learned in Seoul, by Mibu-dera.

    38 Mibu Tsujimachi, Nakagyo-ku, Kyoto, 604-8822, Japan

    Recommended by Michelin ★

  19. Must see · Kaiseki, Kyō-ryōri & Ryōtei · Central

    Manjuji Hakuran

    New One MICHELIN Star 2026 — a Nagasaki-accented Japanese counter in Shimogyō.

    360 Gokuishicho, Shimogyo-ku, Kyoto, 600-8429, Japan

    Recommended by Michelin ★

  20. Must see · International & Fusion · Central

    shiro

    One MICHELIN Star — Japanese technique with modern Italian flavour; the hamo-and-prosciutto is an inspectors' must-try.

    2F, 287 Takoyakushicho, Nakagyo-ku, Kyoto, 604-0021, Japan

    Recommended by Michelin ★

  21. Must see · International & Fusion · Central

    MOKO

    One MICHELIN Star — Alexis Moko (Paris/London-trained) cooking French in an old merchant's house with Kyoto produce.

    235-2 Tamauecho, Nakagyo-ku, Kyoto, 604-0005, Japan

    Recommended by Michelin ★

  22. Must see · Kaiseki, Kyō-ryōri & Ryōtei · Central

    Godan Miyazawa

    One MICHELIN Star (2026) — sister of Jiki Miyazawa; its signature yaki-gomadōfu heralds each season.

    557 Oecho, Shimogyo-ku, Kyoto, 600-8402, Japan

    Recommended by Michelin ★

  23. Must see · Sushi & Kaisen-don · Central

    Kyogoku Kaneyo

    Seven-generation eel house (Michelin Bib Gourmand); Kantō-style steamed-then-grilled kabayaki, famous for the kinshi-don.

    456 Matsugae-chō, Nakagyō-ku, Kyoto, Japan

    Recommended by Michelin Bib

  24. Must see · Kaiseki, Kyō-ryōri & Ryōtei · Central

    Isshisoden Nakamura

    Three MICHELIN Stars (2026); a house that began as a travelling fishmonger, now led by sixth-generation head Motokazu Nakamura.

    136 Matsushita-chō, Nakagyō-ku, Kyoto 604-8093, Japan

    Recommended by Michelin ★

  25. Must see · Kaiseki, Kyō-ryōri & Ryōtei · Central

    Pontocho Masuda

    Michelin-listed obanzai counter on Pontochō serving Kyoto's home-style seasonal dishes.

    200 Shimokoriki-chō, Nakagyō-ku, Kyoto 604-8016, Japan

    Recommended by Michelin

  26. Must see · Izakaya, Yakitori & Yokochō · Central

    Torisaki

    One MICHELIN Star yakitori counter; the name means 'the future of yakitori'.

    292-1 Takoyakushi-chō, Nakagyō-ku, Kyoto

    Recommended by Michelin ★

  27. Must see · International & Fusion · Central

    DODICI

    One MICHELIN Star (2026) Italian: a chef trained in Italy giving the cooking a Japanese essence.

    239 Kamihakusan-chō, Nakagyō-ku, Kyoto 604-0943

    Recommended by Michelin ★

  28. Worth the detour · Central

    Marufukuro — former Nintendo headquarters (丸福樓)

    Nintendo's 1930s original head office (used until 1959), the 'Yamauchi Nintendo' plaques still on the façade, reopened April 2022 as a Tadao Ando-designed hotel; the exterior is viewable from the street.

    Your guide’s note ★ Anime & pop culture — Nintendo — the building where the playing-card firm Marufuku/Yamauchi Nintendo was run before video games.

    342 Kagiya-chō, Shōmen-dōri Kamogawa-nishi-iru, Shimogyō-ku, Kyoto

    Recommended by Time Out, Michelin, Kyotocity

  29. Worth the detour · Central

    Pokémon Center Kyoto (ポケモンセンターキョウト)

    The official Pokémon store in Kyoto, reopened in March 2019 in SUINA Muromachi. A Pikachu dressed as a maiko and the legendary Lugia and Ho-Oh greet visitors, and it sells Kyoto-only goods.

    Your guide’s note ★ Anime & pop culture — Pokémon — official Pokémon Center with Kyoto-exclusive maiko-Pikachu merchandise.

    SUINA Muromachi 2F (Kyoto Economic Center), Shimogyō-ku, Kyoto (direct from Shijō / Karasuma stations)

    Recommended by Walkerplus (kadokawa), Famitsu (kadokawa Game Linkage), Mapple (Shobunsha)

  30. Worth the detour · Central

    Nintendo KYOTO

    Nintendo's third official store in Japan, after Tokyo and Osaka, which opened on 17 October 2023 in its hometown. It has Mario and warp-pipe statues and Mario, Zelda, Splatoon and Animal Crossing merchandise.

    Your guide’s note ★ Anime & pop culture — Nintendo (Mario, Zelda, Splatoon) — the company's official store in its home city.

    Kyoto Takashimaya S.C. [T8] 7F, Shimogyō-ku, Kyoto

    Recommended by Famitsu (kadokawa Game Linkage), Anime News Network, Kyoto Shimbun

  31. Worth the detour · Sushi & Kaisen-don · Central

    Kyo Unawa Honten (京うな和)

    The downtown eel specialist by Nishiki: crisp-skinned Kansai-style grilled unagi.

    Shijō Sakai-machi, Nakagyō-ku, Kyoto (steps from Nishiki Market)

    Recommended by Time Out, Inside Kyoto (Chris Rowthorn), Savor Japan

  32. Worth the detour · Central

    Kyoto Station

    Hiroshi Hara's 1997 glass-and-steel station building, built for the city's 1,200th anniversary — the giant atrium staircase climbs to a free rooftop skyway with city views.

    Shimogyō-ku, Kyoto, Japan

    Recommended by Japan-guide, Kyoto City Tourism

  33. Worth the detour · Central

    Kyoto Tower

    The 131-metre tower opposite Kyoto Station, the city's tallest structure; the observation deck at 100 m gives a 360° view to Osaka on clear days.

    Shimogyō-ku, Kyoto, Japan

    Recommended by Japan-guide, Wikipedia

  34. Worth the detour · Central

    Nishiki Tenmangū

    Small shrine to Sugawara no Michizane at the east end of Nishiki Market, wedged into the Shinkyōgoku shopping arcade — its torii's ends literally run into the neighbouring buildings.

    Nakagyō-ku, Kyoto, Japan

    Recommended by Kyoto City Tourism, Wikipedia

  35. Worth the detour · Central

    Museum of Kyoto

    City history-and-culture museum on Sanjō-dōri, partly housed in the 1906 red-brick former Bank of Japan Kyoto branch; regular film screenings.

    Nakagyō-ku, Kyoto, Japan

    Recommended by Kyoto City Tourism, Wikipedia

  36. Worth the detour · Central

    Rokkaku-dō (Chōhō-ji)

    Hexagonal temple said to be founded by Prince Shōtoku, birthplace of ikebana — the Ikenobō school's headquarters and Ikebana Museum stand in its grounds.

    Nakagyō-ku, Kyoto, Japan

    Recommended by Kyoto City Tourism, Wikipedia

  37. Worth the detour · Central

    Kyoto Aquarium

    Modern inland aquarium (2012) in Umekōji Park, a 15-minute walk west of Kyoto Station, with a Kyoto-rivers zone of Japanese giant salamanders.

    Shimogyō-ku, Kyoto, Japan

    Recommended by Japan-guide, Wikipedia

  38. Worth the detour · Central

    Mibu-dera

    Temple founded in 991 for Jizō, guardian of children, and HQ ground of the Shinsengumi — graves of commander Kondō Isami and members lie in its Mibu-zuka; famous for its Kyōgen mime plays.

    Nakagyō-ku, Kyoto, Japan

    Recommended by Kyoto City Tourism, Japanese Wikipedia (ja.wikipedia.org)

  39. Worth the detour · Central

  82. Deep cut · Central

    Honnō-ji

    Temple rebuilt on Teramachi after the 1582 Honnō-ji Incident, in which Oda Nobunaga died at its original site; his memorial tower stands here.

    Recommended by Kyoto City Tourism, Wikipedia

Kita & Kamigyō 46

Kinkaku-ji · Daitoku-ji · Imperial Palace · Nishijin · Kamigamo

  1. Must see · Kita & Kamigyō

    Daitoku-ji

    Walled Rinzai Zen complex of some two dozen sub-temples — one of the best places in Japan to see a range of Zen gardens and tea culture.

    Kita-ku, Kyoto, Japan

    Recommended by Japan-guide, Wikipedia

  2. Must see · Kita & Kamigyō

    Kitano Tenmangū

    Head of the shrines to the scholar Sugawara no Michizane — students pray here before exams; famous for its plum grove and its monthly flea market on the 25th.

    Kamigyō-ku, Kyoto, Japan

    Recommended by Japan-guide, Wikipedia

  3. Must see · Kita & Kamigyō

    Kyoto Imperial Palace

    The emperors' residence until 1868, inside the vast Kyoto Gyoen park; the palace grounds are free to visit without reservation.

    Kamigyō-ku, Kyoto, Japan

    Recommended by Japan-guide, Wikipedia

  4. Must see · Kita & Kamigyō

    Kamigamo Shrine (Kamo-wake-ikazuchi Jinja)

    One of Kyoto's oldest Shinto shrines, older than the city itself, with its two sand cones (tatesuna) before the Hosodono hall; UNESCO-listed component 688-001.

    Kita-ku, Kyoto, Japan

    Recommended by UNESCO, Wikipedia

  5. Must see · Kita & Kamigyō

    Kinkaku-ji (Rokuon-ji)

    The Golden Pavilion — a gold-leafed Zen reliquary hall over a mirror pond, rebuilt in 1955 after arson; UNESCO 688-013.

    Kita-ku, Kyoto, Japan

    Recommended by UNESCO, Wikipedia

  6. Must see · Wagashi, Matcha & Sweets · Kita & Kamigyō

    Kazariya (かざりや)

    The 'Honke' aburi-mochi house (c.1600), facing Ichiwa across Imamiya Shrine's approach.

    Imamiya Shrine east approach, Murasakino, Kita-ku, Kyoto

    Recommended by Lonely Planet, Leaf Kyoto (京都リーフ)

  7. Must see · Wagashi, Matcha & Sweets · Kita & Kamigyō

    Ichiwa (一和 / 一文字屋和輔)

    Said to be founded in 1000 (Chōhō 2) — among Japan's oldest confectioners; aburi-mochi at Imamiya Shrine's gate.

    Imamiya Shrine east approach, Murasakino, Kita-ku, Kyoto

    Recommended by Leaf Kyoto (京都リーフ), Japanese Wikipedia (ja.wikipedia.org)

  8. Must see · Tofu, Shōjin & Vegetarian · Kita & Kamigyō

    Izusen Daitoku-ji (泉仙 大徳寺)

    Shōjin lunches in a sub-temple garden of Daitoku-ji, served since 1963.

    Within the Daitoku-ji temple complex, Murasakino, Kita-ku, Kyoto

    Recommended by Kyoto City Tourism, Inside Kyoto (Chris Rowthorn)

  9. Must see · Wagashi, Matcha & Sweets · Kita & Kamigyō

    Demachi Futaba (出町ふたば)

    Since 1899 the queue-worthy mame-mochi shop at the old Ōhara road entrance to the city.

    Demachi, Kamigyō-ku, Kyoto (near Demachiyanagi)

    Recommended by Lonely Planet, Matcha — Japan Travel Guide

  10. Must see · Wagashi, Matcha & Sweets · Kita & Kamigyō

    Awamochi-dokoro Sawaya (粟餅所 澤屋)

    A wagashi shop facing Kitano Tenmangū with roughly 340 years of history. Its additive-free millet mochi is made only when ordered and keeps for one day. It is on Tabelog's 2023 Hyakumeiten sweets list.

    In front of Kitano Tenmangū, Kamigyō-ku, Kyoto

    Recommended by Mapple (Shobunsha), Pearl (joinpearl.co)

  11. Must see · Izakaya, Yakitori & Yokochō · Kita & Kamigyō

    Shinba (神馬), Senbon Nakadachiuri

    A popular sakaba (drinking hall) opened in 1934 near Nishijin. Serai calls it the shrine of Kyoto's taishū-sakaba.

    Senbon Nakadachiuri, Kamigyō-ku, Kyoto

    Recommended by Serai (Shogakukan), Rurubu (JTB Publishing, rurubu.jp)

  12. Must see · International & Fusion · Kita & Kamigyō

    KOGA

    One MICHELIN Star (2026; an inspectors' favourite dish) — French in Kamigyō, with ~30 Takagamine vegetables and charcoal-grilled meat.

    230 Nakaogawacho, Kamigyo-ku, Kyoto, 602-0053, Japan

    Recommended by Michelin ★

  13. Must see · Kaiseki, Kyō-ryōri & Ryōtei · Kita & Kamigyō

    MUBE

    New One MICHELIN Star 2026 (inspectors' reveal article) — fermentation-driven Japanese cooking in Kita-ku.

    11-1 Omiya Gentakukitamachi, Kita-ku, Kyoto, 603-8462, Japan

    Recommended by Michelin ★

  14. Must see · Ramen & Tsukemen · Kita & Kamigyō

    Noodle Shop Rennosuke

    Michelin Bib Gourmand noodle bar, relocated from Murasakino (Kita-ku) to Kamigyō-ku; house noodles of Kyoto wheat in a clear seafood-dashi broth seasoned with pure soy sauce.

    116-2 Higashitate-chō, Kamigyō-ku, Kyoto 602-8377, Japan

    Recommended by Michelin Bib

  15. Must see · Kaiseki, Kyō-ryōri & Ryōtei · Kita & Kamigyō

    Doppo

    Two MICHELIN Stars (2026): tea-house interior hung with scrolls; cooking that honours Japanese aesthetics and classical art equally.

    1-1 Izumoji Matsunoshita-chō, Kita-ku, Kyoto 603-8133

    Recommended by Michelin ★

  16. Worth the detour · Kita & Kamigyō

    Demachi Masugata Shōtengai (出町桝形商店街)

    A 164 m retro local arcade at the end of the old Saba Kaidō mackerel road, with the Demachi-za mini-theatre — the real model for the Usagiyama shopping street in Kyoto Animation's Tamako Market.

    Your guide’s note ★ Anime & pop culture — Tamako Market (Kyoto Animation, 2013) — model for Usagiyama Shōtengai; the arcade openly welcomes fans.

    Kamigyō-ku, Kyoto (Demachi, just west of the Kamo River delta)

    Recommended by Wikipedia, Kyoto City Tourism, METI

  17. Worth the detour · Kita & Kamigyō

    Kamishichiken

    Kyoto's oldest geiko district, by Kitano Tenmangū in the Nishijin weaving quarter; its geiko and maiko serve at the shrine's Baikasai plum tea ceremony every 25 February.

    Kamigyō-ku, Kyoto, Japan

    Recommended by Japan-guide, Kyoto City Tourism, Wikipedia

  18. Worth the detour · Kita & Kamigyō

    Ryōgen-in, Daitoku-ji (龍源院)

    Daitoku-ji sub-temple built in 1502, head of the temple's southern school, with as many as five different dry-landscape gardens around its main hall.

    Murasakino, Kita-ku, Kyoto

    Recommended by Japanese Wikipedia (ja.wikipedia.org), Japan-guide, Lonely Planet

  19. Worth the detour · Kita & Kamigyō

    Funaoka Onsen (船岡温泉)

    A sentō opened in 1923 in the former inn Funaoka-rō, registered as a Tangible Cultural Property, the third bathhouse in Japan to be listed. It has a karahafu entrance, carved coffered ceilings, majolica-tiled corridors and Japan's first electric bath.

    Murasakino, Kita-ku, Kyoto

    Recommended by Kyoto City Tourism, Rurubu (JTB Publishing, rurubu.jp), Leaf Kyoto (京都リーフ)

  20. Worth the detour · Kita & Kamigyō

    Kōtō-in

    Daitoku-ji sub-temple famed for its maple-lined bamboo approach and moss garden — one of Kyoto's best autumn-colour spots.

    Kita-ku, Kyoto, Japan

    Recommended by Japan-guide, Wikipedia

  21. Worth the detour · Kita & Kamigyō

    Imamiya Shrine

    Shrine north of Daitoku-ji prayed to for a fortunate marriage ('tama-no-koshi'); at its east gate two rival shops have grilled aburi-mochi rice cakes for centuries.

    Kita-ku, Kyoto, Japan

    Recommended by Kyoto City Tourism, Wikipedia

  22. Worth the detour · Kita & Kamigyō

    Seimei Shrine

    Shrine to Abe no Seimei, the Heian court diviner (onmyōji), marked by star-pentagram crests; a pilgrimage spot for fans of onmyōji fiction.

    Kamigyō-ku, Kyoto, Japan

    Recommended by Kyoto City Tourism, Wikipedia

  23. Worth the detour · Kita & Kamigyō

    Hirano Shrine

    Ancient shrine near Kitano Tenmangū, long one of Kyoto's classic cherry-blossom (hanami) spots.

    Kita-ku, Kyoto, Japan

    Recommended by Kyoto City Tourism, Wikipedia

  24. Worth the detour · Kita & Kamigyō

    Sentō Imperial Palace

    Retired Emperor Go-Mizunoo's 1630 palace in Kyoto Gyoen; free guided tours through its North and South Pond stroll gardens.

    Kamigyō-ku, Kyoto, Japan

    Recommended by Japan-guide, Wikipedia

  25. Worth the detour · Kita & Kamigyō

    Genkō-an

    Takagamine Zen temple famous for its two windows on the garden — the square 'Window of Confusion' and round 'Window of Enlightenment' — and a 'blood ceiling' of floorboards from Fushimi Castle.

    Kita-ku, Kyoto, Japan

    Recommended by Kyoto City Tourism, Japanese Wikipedia (ja.wikipedia.org)

  26. Worth the detour · Kita & Kamigyō

    Shōden-ji

    Quiet temple in the northern hills whose dry garden of clipped azaleas borrows distant Mount Hiei as scenery; another Fushimi Castle 'blood ceiling'.

    Kita-ku, Kyoto, Japan

    Recommended by Kyoto City Tourism, Japanese Wikipedia (ja.wikipedia.org)

  27. Worth the detour · Kita & Kamigyō

    Kōetsu-ji

    Nichiren temple on land Tokugawa Ieyasu granted the artist Hon'ami Kōetsu for his arts colony in Takagamine; known for its bamboo 'Kōetsu fence' and maples.

    Kita-ku, Kyoto, Japan

    Recommended by Japan-guide, Japanese Wikipedia (ja.wikipedia.org)

  28. Worth the detour · Kita & Kamigyō

    Shingon temple founded in 1221 whose Main Hall (Shakadō) is the oldest standing Buddhist hall in Kyoto — a National Treasure that survived the Ōnin War.

    Kamigyō-ku, Kyoto, Japan

    Recommended by Kyoto City Tourism, Wikipedia

  29. Worth the detour · Kita & Kamigyō

    Recommended by Kyoto City Tourism, Wikipedia
